Rashi on Arakhin 30a:12:1.english: And [the field] appreciated - on its own:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:12:2.hebrew: העודף שבידו - הנשאר בידו מן הדמים שקיבל, לאחר שינכה לו הלוקח חשבון המגיע לכל שנה שאכלה:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:12:2.english: The remainder that is in his possession - [That is,] what remains in his possession from the money that he received, after the buyer deducts for him the amount corresponding to each year that he consumed [the produce of] it:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:13:1.english: It depreciated - it deteriorated and its value decreased:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:13:2.hebrew: שבקרקע - עודף שהקרקע שוה יותר על מה שמגיע לחשבון שמנכה לו הלוקח לשנים שאכלה, דהאי "עודף" איכא למדרש להכי ולהכי:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:13:2.english: [That which is] in the land - [meaning] the excess that the land is worth beyond what amounts to the calculation that the buyer deducts for him for the years that he ate [its produce], for this [word] "remainder" can be expounded in this way and in that way:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:14:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - בין רבי לר' דוסתאי? מ"מ, בין למר בין למר לקולא אזלינן:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:14:1.english: What is [the practical difference] between them - [i.e.,] between Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and Rabbi Dostai [ben Yehuda]? In any event, according to both this one and that one, we follow the leniency:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:14:2.hebrew: כגון דאייקר וזל ואייקר - שמכרה לו במאתים, ומכרה ראשון לשני במנה, ונתייקרה ביד השני ועמדה על מאתים. לרבי, דאמר "לאיש אשר בתוכה" — לא יהיב אלא מנה, כמה דיהיב בה שני. לר' דוסתאי — יהיב מאתים, דאי אמרת עודף שבידו, הא מאתן שקיל מקמא; ואי אמרת עודף שבקרקע, הא מאתן שויא:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:14:2.english: For example, where it was high, and depreciated, and appreciated - Where he [the original owner] sold it to him [the first buyer] for two hundred [zuz], and the first [buyer] sold it to a second [buyer] for a maneh [one hundred zuz], and it appreciated in the possession of the second [buyer] and stood at two hundred. According to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who says [that the verse refers] "to the man who is in it" — he [the original owner] only pays a maneh, as much as the second [buyer] paid for it. According to Rabbi Dostai — he pays two hundred: for if you say [it is calculated according to] the surplus in his hand, behold, he took two hundred from the first [buyer]; and if you say [it is calculated according to] the surplus in the land, behold, it is worth two hundred:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:16:1.hebrew: גאולה גאולה - כתיב הכא (ויקרא כ״ה:כ״ו) "ומצא כדי גאולתו", וכתיב בעבד עברי (שם) "גאולה תהיה לו":
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:16:1.english: “Redemption” [and] “redemption” - It is written here (Leviticus 25:26): “and he finds sufficient means for its redemption,” and it is written regarding a Hebrew slave (ibid.): “he shall have redemption”:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:17:1.hebrew: אלא ממנה - כשבא לפדות עצמו, מחשב כמה שנים משעה שנמכר (עד שנת היובל), ומחשב כמה מגיע מאותו מנה לכל שנה ושנה; ואם עברו שתים או שלש שנים, ינכה לו אדוניו לפי חשבון המגיע לכל שנה, כדכתיב: "כימי שכיר יהיה עמו":
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:17:1.english: Only from a maneh - When he comes to redeem himself, he calculates how many years [there are] from the time he was sold (until the Jubilee year), and he calculates how much of that maneh comes to each and every year; and if two or three years have passed, his master deducts for him according to the calculation of what comes to each year, as it is written: "like the days of a hired laborer shall he be with him":

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:18:1.hebrew: כפי שניו - משמע כפי שנים שעמד בהן, כלומר לפי מה שהוא שוה באותה שעה:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:18:1.english: According to his years - [This] implies: according to the years in which he [now] stands, that is to say, according to what he is worth at that time:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:19:1.hebrew: אין לי וכו' - דהאי קרא בנמכר לעובד כוכבים כתיב, כדכתיב (שם): "וכי תשיג יד גר ותושב" וכו':
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:19:1.english: I have [derived] only, etc. - For this verse is written regarding one who is sold to a gentile, as it is written (there): "And if a stranger or a resident alien acquires means," etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:19:2.hebrew: שכיר שכיר - כתיב הכא (שם): "כימי שכיר יהיה עמו", וכתיב בנמכר לישראל (דברים ט״ו:י״ח): "כי משנה שכר שכיר עבדך" וגו':
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:19:2.english: “Hired worker,” “hired worker” - It is written here (there [Leviticus 25:50]) [regarding a slave sold to a gentile]: “According to the time of a hired worker shall he be with him,” and it is written regarding [one] sold to a Jew (Deuteronomy 15:18): “For double the hire of a hired worker he served you,” etc.:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:1:1.hebrew: ורב ענן - דהוה מספקא ליה בהי הדרי ובהי לא הדרי, הך ברייתא ד"צריך גט שיחרור" לא הוה שמיעא ליה; ומהא דאמר שמואל "אינה מכורה" לא הוה מצי למשמע מידי, דממאי דאינה מכורה ומעות חוזרין? דלמא מעות שנתן לוקח למוכר מתנה הן ביד מוכר, ואיכא בין רב לשמואל הך דפרישית לעיל:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:1:1.english: And Rav Anan - who was in doubt regarding which [case the money] returns and regarding which it does not return, had not heard this baraita [which states] that [the slave] "requires a bill of manumission"; and from that which Shmuel said, "[the field] is not sold," he could not infer anything, for from where [is it known] that it is not sold and [that] the money returns? Perhaps the money that the buyer gave to the seller is a gift in the seller's possession, and the [difference] between Rav and Shmuel is that [matter] which I explained above:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:1:2.hebrew: ומעות חוזרין - דאדם יודע שאין קדושין תופסין באחותו, וגמר ונתן לשם פקדון; ולשמואל, גמר ונתן לשם מתנה:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:1:2.english: And the money is returned - [This is] because a person knows that betrothal does not take effect with his sister, and he resolved and gave [it] as a deposit; whereas according to Shmuel, he resolved and gave [it] as a gift:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:2:1.hebrew: דקנסת ללוקח - גבי מוכר עבדו בחוצה לארץ, דאמרי' לא הדרי זביני, ויוצא עבד לחירות ומפסיד לוקח:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:2:1.english: That you penalize the buyer - [This refers to the case] regarding one who sells his slave outside of the Land [of Israel], where we say [that] the purchase money is not returned, and the slave goes free, and the buyer loses [his money]:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:2:2.hebrew: ליקנסיה למוכר - שיהו מעות חוזרין, ויוציאו מוכר לחירות:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:2:2.english: Let us penalize the seller - [Meaning] that the money should be returned [to the buyer], and the seller should free him:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:3:1.hebrew: לאו עכברא גנב - עכבר הגונב ומניח בחוץ, אם לא היה לו חור להניח בו לא היה גונב; הלכך חורא גנבא וקא גניב ליה. ה"נ, אם לא היה מוצא לוקח לא היה מוכרו:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:3:1.english: It is not the mouse that steals - A mouse that steals and leaves [it] outside, if it did not have a hole to put [it] in, it would not steal; therefore, the hole is the thief and steals it. So too here, if [the seller] had not found a buyer, he would not have sold him.

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:3:2.english: The hole, from where [does it] have [it] - From where does the hole have the stolen item:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:3:3.hebrew: דאיתא לאיסורא - דהיינו לוקח, שהעבד אצלו:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:3:3.english: [Where] the prohibited [item] is - That is, the buyer, in whose possession the slave is:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:5:1.hebrew: [הב ליה דמיה - פי' דמי הניר, קמ"ל]:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:5:1.english: Give him its value - Meaning, the value of the plowing; [the Mishnah] teaches us [that we do not say so]:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:6:1.hebrew: שלא יאמר - מוכר הבא לפדותה לסוף שתי שנים: "הנח לפני מליאה פירות, כדרך שהנחתי לפניך כשמכרתי לך":
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:6:1.english: That [he] should not say - [Namely,] the seller who comes to redeem it at the end of two years [should not say to the buyer]: "Leave [it] before me full of produce, in the manner that I left [it] before you when I sold [it] to you."

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:6:2.hebrew: במספר שני תבואות - משמע כל תבואות שבשתי שנים, מדהוה ליה למיכתב "מספר שנים" או "מספר תבואות", דהוי משמע שתי תבואות:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:6:2.english: According to the number of years of the crops - [This] implies all crops in two years, since it could have written "the number of years" or "the number of crops," which would have implied [only] two crops:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:7:1.hebrew: אינו מחשב - המוכר כשבא לגאלה, אלא עם הראשון; ומחשב כמה שנים היו משמכרה לו עד שנת היובל, ומחשב כמה מגיע מן המנה לכל שנה, ולפי אותו חשבון ינכה לו לוקח לכל שנה ושנה שאכלה, והמותר יחזיר לו:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:7:1.english: He does not calculate - [that is,] the seller, when he comes to redeem it, [calculates] only with the first [buyer]; and he calculates how many years there were from when he sold it to him until the Jubilee year, and he calculates how much of the maneh [one hundred dinars] corresponds to each year, and according to that calculation the buyer deducts for him for each and every year that he consumed [its produce], and the remainder [the seller] returns to him:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:7:2.hebrew: [לאיש] אשר מכר לו - "והשיב את העודף לאיש וגו'", בגואל שדה ממכרו כתיב:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:7:2.english: [To the man] to whom he sold it - "And he shall return the remainder to the man, etc." — [this] is written regarding one who redeems a field from his sale:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:8:1.hebrew: לאיש אשר בתוכה - ובגמ' פריך: מנלן דדרשינן לקולא? לידרוש לחומרא:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:8:1.english: To the man who is in it - And in the Gemara it asks: From where do we [know] that we expound [this] leniently? Let us expound [it] stringently:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:9:1.english: He may not sell a distant field - that he has, in order to redeem this [field] that is near to him. In the Gemara, it explains from where we [derive this]:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:9:2.english: And he may not borrow - money in order to redeem it:

Rashi on Arakhin 30a:9:3.hebrew: מותר בכולן - המקדיש שדהו, מותר למכור שדה אחרת או ללות כדי לגאלה, וגואל לחצאין — אם אינו מספיק לגאול את כולה, יגאל חציה, ולכשיוכל יגאלנה כולה:
Rashi on Arakhin 30a:9:3.english: [It is] permitted in all of these [ways] - One who consecrates his field is permitted to sell another field or to borrow [money] in order to redeem it, and he may redeem [it] in halves — if he does not have enough to redeem all of it, he may redeem half of it, and when he is able, he may redeem all of it:

Tosafot on Arakhin 30a:14:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו דאייקר וזל ואייקר - ה"ה דהוה מצי למימר דאייקר וזל בלוקח אחד בלבד; דאילו לרבי, דלא דריש "העודף", בין לאיש אשר מכר בין לאיש אשר בתוכה, צריך לגואלה כפי המכר, דהיינו ביוקר, ולרבי דוסתאי ברבי יהודה, אזלינן בתר העלוי שבקרקע, ונגאלת כפי העלוי. אלא לפי דאיירי במתניתין בשני מוכרין, ניחא ליה למינקט נמי איכא בינייהו בשני מוכרין:
Tosafot on Arakhin 30a:14:1.english: There is [a practical difference] between them where it was high, depreciated, and appreciated - The same applies that [the Gemara] could have said "where it was high and depreciated" with a single buyer alone. For according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who does not expound [the word] "the remainder" — whether [sold] to the man to whom he sold [it] or to the man who is [currently] in it — he must redeem it according to the sale [price], which is at the high price; whereas according to Rabbi Dostai ben Rabbi Yehuda, we follow the [current] value in the land, and it is redeemed according to that value. Rather, because it speaks in our Mishnah of two sellers, [the Gemara] preferred to state the practical difference between them [in a case] of two sellers as well:

Tosafot on Arakhin 30a:1:1.hebrew: דלמא אינה מכורה ומעות מתנה מידי דהוה אמקדש אחותו - ומיהו לפי האמת שהוכחנו דמעות חוזרים, אמרי' דלא דמי למקדש אחותו, לפי שאדם יודע שאין קדושין תופסין באחותו, וגמר ונתן לשם מתנה; אבל במוכר שדהו בשנת היובל, אין העולם בקיאין בכך, ולא גמר לשום מתנה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 30a:1:1.english: Perhaps [it] is not sold and [the] money is a gift, just as in [the case of] one who betroths his sister - However, according to the truth that we have proved, that the money is returned, we say that [this] is not comparable to one who betroths his sister; for a person knows that betrothal does not take effect with his sister, and [therefore] he resolved and gave [it] as a gift, whereas with one who sells his field in the Jubilee Year, people are not well-versed in this, and he did not resolve [to give it] as a gift:

Tosafot on Arakhin 30a:9:1.hebrew: לא ימכור ברחוק ויגאול בקרוב - ה"ה איפכא דלא, אלא אורחא דמילתא נקט:
Tosafot on Arakhin 30a:9:1.english: One may not sell in a distant [area] and redeem in a nearby [area] - The same applies in the reverse [case], that [he may] not [do so]; rather, [the Tanna] stated the usual way of things:
